To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a large lump sum tax is a necessary and sufficient condition to obtain local and global indeterminate equilibria and limit cycles in a model of endogenous growth with public capital and congestion.
the endogenous labor supply and the congestion effect of public capital services on the economic growth are the main ingredients to obtain complex dynamic behavior in an endogenous growth model.
a large lumpsum tax is necessary to obtain complex equilibrium dynamics in a model where public capital is congested and labor supply is endogeneous.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the dynamic equilibrium of an economy in which the labor supply is determined endogenously and the growth is sustained by the public investment.
a model where public capital is endogenous and its services are congested.
the effects of fiscal policy on the long-run equilibrium and the dynamic equilibrium of the economy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in this model, fiscal policy is a key determinant for the existence and the number of balanced-growth paths.
the existence of multiple balanced-growth equilibria is not a rare phenomenon in economic growth models.
the presence of public capital, together with a large lump-sum taxation, is a necessary condition for the existence of multiple balanced-growth path equilibria and limit cycles in the model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a large tax is necessary to generate complex dynamics and that this complexity is associated with the endogenous labor supply.
a fiscal policy with large lump-sum taxes and a small public capital stock is able to generate a complex dynamic equilibrium.
the endogenous growth in a model with public capital can be very sensitive to the fiscal policy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the presence of multiple equilibria and indeterminacy in a model with endogenous labor supply and endogenous growth may be more likely when there are public capital services that are congested by households but not by the number of units of time they work.
the presence of a public good in an economy may lead to complex dynamics, and that the fiscal policies may play a key role in the determination of the long-run growth rate.

the endogenous-growth models that assume that the public capital services increase the economic productivity may exhibit a richer dynamic equilibrium behavior than the ones that assume that the economic productivity depends on the stock of public capital.
